Traditional Noodle Kugel

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement) · Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)

Serves 8Prep 20 minCook 1 hr

Kugel is a classic Jewish casserole typically made with noodles or potatoes, served during significant holidays such as Yom Kippur and Hanukkah. On Yom Kippur, it is often eaten before the fast begins, while during Hanukkah, its comforting, baked nature complements the festive meals celebrating the Festival of Lights.

Ingredients

  • 12 oz (340 g) wide egg noodles
  • 6 large eggs
  • 1 cup (240 ml) sour cream
  • 1 cup (240 ml) cottage cheese
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (115 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) raisins (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (50 g) crushed cornflakes or breadcrumbs for topping

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.
  2. Cook the egg noodles according to package instructions until al dente, then drain and set aside.
  3. In a large mixing bowl, beat the eggs and then add sour cream, cottage cheese, sugar, melted butter, vanilla extract, salt, and cinnamon. Mix until well combined.
  4. Fold the cooked noodles and raisins (if using) into the egg mixture until evenly coated.
  5. Pour the noodle mixture into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly.
  6. Sprinkle the crushed cornflakes or breadcrumbs evenly over the top for a crunchy topping.
  7. Bake uncovered for about 1 hour, or until the kugel is set and the top is golden brown.
  8. Remove from oven and let cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For a dairy-free version, substitute sour cream and cottage cheese with plant-based alternatives.
  • Add a pinch of nutmeg for extra warmth and flavor.
  • Serve warm or at room temperature; kugel can be refrigerated and reheated.
